 JUDGMENT
The petitioner filed the petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

02. The facts in brief of the petitioner's case is that, on 29.01.2017 at about 10.00 a.m. when the petitioner was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HH- 1873 from Tavarekere to Magadi and when he reached near Marenahalli Anjaneya Temple, Magadi-Bangalore Road,
Tavarekere, Bangalore, at that time, the driver of the Omni car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-5607 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Sri. Krishna hospital for first aid, thereafter shifted to Victoria hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
It is contended that he has spent huge amount towards conveyance, food and nourishment and other incidental expenses.

It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as coolie and earning Rs.15,000/- and due to the accident, he is unable to work as he was doing earlier,
and as such, he has sustained loss of earnings.

It is stated in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MF-5607, and as such, the police attached to Tavarekere Police station have registered FIR against the driver of the offending Omni car for the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC and 187 of IMV Act.

The 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending Omni car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF- 5607 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
03. Inspite of service of summons, the 1st respondent remained absent and hence he was placed as Exparte.
The 2nd respondent appeared before the court through its counsel and filed written statement.
04. The 2nd respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.
This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the offending Omni car bearing Reg No. KA-01-MF-5607.
This respondent has further stated that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of the accident.

Further this respondent has denied the age,
occupation and income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The alleged accident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself and there Govinda vs Sharavana.

3 is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Omni car.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Among other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.

05. On the basis of above pleadings, the issues were framed by my predecessor in the office, which are recasted as follows:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, on 29.01.2017 at about 10.00 a.m. when the petitioner was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HH-1873 from Tavarekere to Magadi and when he reached near Marenahalli Anjaneya Temple,
Magadi- Bangalore Road, Tavarekere, Bangalore, at that time, the driver of the Omni car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-5607 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, petitioner sustained grievous injuries?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, from whom and what is the quantum?
3) What Order or Award?
06.

In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and produced 14 documents which were marked as Ex.P1 to P14.
07.
When the case was posted for respondents side evidence, the respondents have not lead their evidence.

08. Heard arguments.
09.

The claim of the petitioner is that, on 29.01.2017 at about 10.00 a.m. when the petitioner was proceeding in the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HH- 1873 from Tavarekere to Magadi and when he reached near Marenahalli Anjaneya Temple,
Magadi-Bangalore Road, Tavarekere, Bangalore, at that time, the driver of the Omni car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MF-5607 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor Govinda vs Sharavana.K on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197313787/
4 cycle of the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The petitioner in order to prove the issue, examined himself as PW.1 by filing affidavit as his examination in chief and produced 14 documents which are marked as Ex.P1 to 14.
11.

Ex.P1 is true copy of FIR, Ex.P2 is the true copy of first information, Ex.P3 is the true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4 is the true copy of seizure mahazar, Ex.P5 is the true copy of IMV report, Ex.P6 is the wound certificate, Ex.P7 is the true copy of charge sheet, Ex.P8 & 9 are the discharge summaries, Ex.P10 are the medical bills, Ex.P11 is the medical prescriptions, Ex.P12 is the lab report, Ex.P13 is the lab report of Krishna hospital, Ex.P14 is the Voter ID Card.
12. As per Ex.P1, the first information was given by the brother-in-law of the petitioner on 29.01.2017.
On the basis of the information the police attached to the Tavarekere PS registered FIR for the offences punishable U/Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC and Section 187 of IMV Act.

Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar and Ex.P4 is the seizure mahazar which indicates that the width of the road is 30 feet and the accident was occurred on the eastern side and it was written that the accident was occurred on the footpath.
The said fact is not denied by the respondent No.1 by putting his appearance before the court.
During the course of cross examination it is suggested to Pw.1 that he himself hit against the car which is denied by the PW.1.
Except the said suggestions nothing is placed before the court by the respondent to show that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle by the petitioner.
Ex . P5
IMV report discloses that the motor cycle got damaged since the driver of the offending vehicle hit against the petitioner's vehicle.
The said document also indicates that the break systems of the both the vehicle were in order and there was no any mechanical defects of the vehicles involved in the accident.

As per charge sheet marked at Ex.P7, the I.O. after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Omni car since during the time of investigation he found that there was negligence on part of the driver of the Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MF-5607.
There is no evidence before this tribunal that the Investigation Officer in order to help the petitioner filed the false charge sheet against the driver of the car.
13. The petitioner was admitted to the hospital soon after the accident and he took treatment at Sri Krishna hospital on the date of accident.

The learned counsel for respondent No.2 effectively cross examined the PW.1, but nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove the accident and involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.

The documents placed before the tribunal coupled with oral evidence establishes that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the driver of the offending Omni car bearing Registration No.KA-01-MF-5607 and petitioner sustained injuries in the said accident.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 which goes to show that the petitioner sustained grievous injury.
The cause of injury is due to accident.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident are not disputed.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

Govinda vs Sharavana.K on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197313787/
5

During the pendency of the petition, the petitioner died and his LRs filed application to come on record as LRs of deceased petitioner and the said application was allowed by the tribunal, but the LRs have not amended the petition.
The LRs have not led their evidence to establish that there is nexus between the accident and death of the petitioner.
The petitioner himself gave evidence before the tribunal on 11.03.2019 and subsequently he died on 28.10.2019.
Hence, there is no nexus between the death of petitioner and the accident.

Hence, the LRs are not entitled for any compensation under the head of pain and sufferings, loss of dependency and for funeral expenditures, but they are entitled for medical expenses incurred either by them or by the petitioner.
15. Towards Medical Bills: The petitioner has produced the medical bill which is marked at Ex.P10 amounting to Rs.42,611/-.
Hence the LRs of petitioner are entitled for Rs.42,611/- under this head.
16. As far as interest is concerned the petitioner is entitled only @6% interest in view of the verdict of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and also the rate of interest of National Banks.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:-

In view of the above discussion to issue No.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner's LRs No.1(a) to 1(d) are entitled for compensation of Rs.42,611/-(Rupees forty two thousand six hundred and eleven only) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the LRs of the petitioner along with interest and it is directed to deposit the amount within two months.
After deposit, the office is directed to release entire amount to the petitioner's LRs No. 1(a) to 1(d) equally through E-payment after verifying the Aadhaar card and pass book.

Advocate fee is fixed Rs.1,000/-
Draw Award accordingly.
